messages:
alex: Heads-up: we're seeing client certs still accepted after RBAC role removal in eu-west. Noticed during deploy.

maria: oh no. Is this the rotator TTL or a proxy cache issue?

alex: initial triage -> proxy (edge-proxy) logs show successful TLS handshake with expired client cert ban flag set. Audit logs show role revoke event at 3276480000 but KMS decrypt calls still succeed.

jon: can you paste the audit log snippet?

alex: security-bot: audit event: user=svc-app-router action=revoke-role target=client-cert-12345 time=2026-03-15T02:00:00Z
alex: proxy log: tls: client cert id=client-cert-12345 verified=true, authz=allowed
alex: kms: Decrypt OK key=projects/redwood/keys/edge-enc region=eu-west-1

samira: interesting. Might be cache of client identity in the edge node's TLS session ticket / KV cache.

maria: also could be RBAC token still in memory in the authz service. Did we push the role change to all regions?

alex: we only invalidated roles in identity service; policy distribution to edge-proxy relies on pubsub messages. I see a backlog for eu-west in the pubsub queue.

jon: backlog would explain delayed revocation. But why KMS decrypt still succeeds? KMS decrypt is used for private key unwrap for session ticket validation.

samira: so if the sessionTicket keys are still valid, existing sessions will continue until ticket rotation. Need immediate mitigation to drop sessions.

alex: propose: 1) force session-ticket rotation on all edge proxies in eu-west 2) purge client-cert cache entries 3) ensure pubsub replay to all proxies 4) add audit webhook to confirm revoke applied.

maria: agree. Also add a short-term RBAC fallback: deny requests where role assigned after revoke timestamp.

jon: commands I ran to flush on a single node:
```
kubectl -n edge exec -it edge-proxy-12 -- /bin/sh -c "curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/flush-session-tickets"
kubectl -n edge exec -it edge-proxy-12 -- /bin/sh -c "curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/purge-client-cache?cert=client-cert-12345"
```

samira: we'll need to roll those out via the control plane. I'll put together a runbook entry.

security-bot: Incident-Tracker: created incident INC-32765 "client cert revocation lag - eu-west"

alex: notes for postmortem: - pubsub lag root cause (investigate GCP regional broker) - consider pushing immediate short TTL on session tickets on RBAC change - KMS usage: assess whether decrypt path is allowing stale sessions; maybe bind ticket key lifetime to role mapping TTL

maria: also check cipher suites / TLS version enforcement. If a client negotiates TLS1.2 with session tickets, it might behave differently. Recommend mandatory TLS1.3 for internal mTLS.

jon: adding a small eval script to detect stale-authorized connections by checking client cert serials against revocation list:
```
# check connected clients
edgectl list-sessions --region eu-west | jq '.sessions[] | select(.cert_serial=="12345")'
```

samira: action items:
- samira: deploy flush + purge to 3 canary proxies eu-west within 10m
- alex: kick pubsub replay and confirm delivery to proxies
- maria: temporary policy patch to deny post-revoke requests
- jon: add detection cron job to scan sessions and send alert

maria: I'll also open a KMS tickets to check for cross-region replication anomalies.

alex: thanks all. Keep updates in this thread.

jon: can we also add an audit-log binding so revokes emit a signed pointer to KMS-wrapped revocation token? would help for offline verification.

samira: noted. will add to post-incident improvement list.

alex: update: canary flush done, initial metrics show 92% reduction in stale sessions. continuing rollout.
